name: Glycogen synthesis
summary: Liver and skeletal muscle in the fed state (insulin). Glucose-6-phosphate → glucose-1-phosphate → UDP-glucose, which glycogen synthase (rate-limiting) adds to a growing α-1,4 chain on a glycogenin primer; branching enzyme moves chain segments onto α-1,6 links. Insulin activates glycogen synthase by dephosphorylation (protein phosphatase 1); glucagon (liver) and epinephrine inactivate it by PKA phosphorylation. Branching enzyme deficiency = Andersen disease (GSD IV).

g6p.name: Glucose-6-phosphate
g6p.notes: From glucose via hexokinase (muscle) or glucokinase (liver). Also allosterically activates glycogen synthase.

udpglc.name: UDP-glucose
udpglc.notes: The activated glucose donor; also feeds galactose metabolism and glucuronidation.

glycogen.name: Glycogen
glycogen.notes: Each UDP-glucose adds one residue by an α-1,4 bond. A new molecule needs the primer protein glycogenin.

branched.name: Branched glycogen
branched.notes: Branches (α-1,6) every ~8–10 residues make glycogen compact and give many ends for fast release.

pgm.name: Phosphoglucomutase
pgm.notes: Reversible; the same enzyme works in glycogenolysis.

ugp.name: UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase
ugp.notes: PPi is hydrolyzed by pyrophosphatase, which pulls the reaction forward.

gys.name: Glycogen synthase
gys.notes: Rate-limiting. Activated by insulin (dephosphorylation via PP1), G6P; inhibited by glucagon and epinephrine (PKA phosphorylation). Makes α-1,4 bonds only.

gbe.name: Branching enzyme
gbe.notes: Moves a block of ~6–7 residues from an α-1,4 chain onto an α-1,6 link. Deficiency = Andersen disease (GSD IV): hepatosplenomegaly, failure to thrive, early cirrhosis and death in early childhood.
